changelog.title: What's new
changelog.subtitle: Every update, newest first.
changelog.r1300.1: The History totals now show Cost (the gil spent on maps) and Revenue (the gil looted, plus the rare loot's worth when loot prices are on, with the net below it), and they count the run under way map by map. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1300.2: Each map's loot list in the History stats now starts folded: click the map's card to open it. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1300.3: Mitigate tankbusters now answers a treasure dungeon boss's tankbuster in time with your short mitigation plus one bigger cooldown, strongest first. While it is on, it handles your personal mitigations itself, so a pack of mobs gets at most one bigger cooldown every 20 seconds instead of all of them. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1300.4: Fixed the Gambler's Lure: a tied guess no longer reads as the end of the lure, so the run waits for the new cards instead of walking off to the locked gate. Challenge by the loot now takes the treasure as it is when the coffer holds rare loot you keep, and only that choice guesses for you. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1300.5: With Kill the mandragora party in order off, mandragoras pulled in by an area attack are now left for last while other enemies are up, and a coffer or gate left targeted no longer stalls a fight. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1300.6: Auto-discard now also discards looted copies of an item that does not stack when your bags already held one, and an item link in chat can be added to the cleanup whitelist from its right-click menu. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1300.7: The chat now says the run is buying on another world only when it really travels there; when no other world qualifies, the run waits out the busy market board instead. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1200.1: Added Chat commands to the settings: list your own commands, one per line (such as /li home or /ays m), and they run when a run finishes on its own, before the after-run action, never after Stop or a failure
changelog.r1200.2: Fixed a run waiting at a hub aetheryte forever when none of the aethernet stops into a zone are attuned, as with the Idyllshire gates to the Hinterlands: it now stops with a message saying a stop needs attuning
changelog.r1200.3: The main window now moves only when you drag its top bar, so a drag inside it no longer moves it by accident; turn on Drag from anywhere in the settings for the old behaviour
changelog.r1100.1: Added treasure dungeons (experimental): with Enter the portal on under Dungeons (off by default), a solo run walks into the portal a map turns up, clears Cenote Ja Ja Gural or the Vault Oneiron, then moves on to the next map; /atm dig does the same. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1100.2: In treasure dungeons the run follows the glowing gate hint or a gate side you pick, fights a boss's adds before the boss, collects the bonus round's sacks and leaves the mandragora party alone unless you ask; Attack bonus enemies first can now be set per dungeon. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1100.3: Added a Gambler's Lure choice for treasure dungeons: Let me choose (the default) waits out the whole lure and suggests the better guess in chat, Open the coffer skips the game, and Challenge by the loot plays it on each card's odds, more carefully when the coffer holds rare loot you keep. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1100.4: Added Buy on the cheapest world (off by default): with Lifestream installed, the run checks Universalis and buys maps on another world of your data centre when that saves enough gil, skips worlds whose listings are over 12 hours old, and goes back to its starting world when the run ends. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1100.5: Added Buy a map ahead and Buy a spare before the first dig (both off by default), so back-to-back maps need fewer trips to the market board, and a busy market board is now waited out instead of ending the visit. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1100.6: Coffer guards go down faster, as the combat preset now spreads area attacks over the whole wave, and the new Mitigate tankbusters setting (off by default) uses a tank's short mitigation near the end of a heavy cast. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1100.7: Added per-map stats on the Treasure and History pages, and a Map log in History with each map's portal, dungeon floor, deaths, time and rare loot; tomestones are now counted on their own, like gil. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1100.8: Added Loot cleanup (off by default): it discards the low-value items coffers and dungeons drop, never anything you already held, keeps whitelisted and notable items, and lets you pick per map and per dungeon which rare loot to keep. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1100.9: Hovering a map name in the map settings or the market price caps shows the game's item tooltip, each map shows the patch it arrived in, and the /atm help lists one command per line. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1100.10: Fixed digs attempted in mid-air after a flying dismount, and, on the Chinese client, coffers left unopened after their guards fell and missing characters in map, city and loot names. Contributed by blackappleD
changelog.r1100.11: Fixed long sessions ending in a crash or a Start button that stops working; moving around no longer sets up new game hooks each time
changelog.r1000.1: Runs your timeworn maps from start to finish: deciphers each one, flies to the dig spot, digs up the coffer, fights off its guards and loots it
changelog.r1000.2: Reads the exact dig spot of the map you hold, shows it on the Treasure page and flags it on your map
changelog.r1000.3: Lets you choose which map tiers a run uses and in what order; undersea maps stay off and 8-player maps carry a warning
changelog.r1000.4: Gathers your daily timeworn map as a Miner or Botanist, switching gearsets there and back
changelog.r1000.5: Buys maps on the market board under a price cap per tier, a budget per run and a gil reserve you set
changelog.r1000.6: Ends a run when you are out of maps, after a set number of maps or minutes, or after repeated failures
changelog.r1000.7: Repairs, eats and takes city breaks between maps, with random reaction delays from the Humanizer
changelog.r1000.8: Records every run in History: maps, coffers, portals seen, gil gained and gil spent
changelog.r1000.9: Leaves treasure dungeon portals alone for now
about.support.title: Made with love and care
about.support.body: This plugin is a one-person project, built in my free time because I love this game and its community. Keeping it updated takes a lot of those hours. If it has helped you, supporting me on Patreon or buying me a coffee means I can keep giving it that time. Thank you for being here.

about.reminder.1: Been at it a while? Roll your shoulders and take one slow breath.
about.reminder.2: Hydration check. When did you last drink some water?
about.reminder.3: Blink a few times and let your eyes rest for a moment.
about.reminder.4: Stand up, stretch, and shake out your hands. Future you says thanks.
about.reminder.5: Sit up and settle in comfortably. Your back will thank you later.
about.reminder.6: Remember to eat something today. You matter more than any score.
about.reminder.7: Eyes feel tired? Look at something far away for twenty seconds.
about.reminder.8: Whatever you're chasing, you're allowed to take a break whenever.
about.reminder.9: You're doing great. Be a little kinder to yourself today.
about.reminder.10: A glass of water and a quick stretch can reset a long session.
about.reminder.11: Unclench your jaw and drop your shoulders. There you go.
about.reminder.12: Rest is part of the journey too. Step away whenever you need to.
about.facts.1: Honey never spoils. Jars over 3,000 years old have been found still edible.
about.facts.2: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.
about.facts.3: A day on Venus is longer than a whole year on Venus.
about.facts.4: Bananas are berries, but strawberries aren't.
about.facts.5: There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe.
about.facts.6: Sharks have been around longer than trees have.
about.facts.7: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
about.facts.8: Honeybees can recognize individual human faces.
about.facts.10: The Eiffel Tower can grow over 15 cm taller on a hot day.
about.facts.11: Hot water can sometimes freeze faster than cold water.

about.quotes.1: Done is better than perfect. You can always polish later.
about.quotes.2: Small steps every day add up to surprising distances.
about.quotes.3: Comparison is the thief of joy. Run your own race.

about.quotes.6: Be patient with yourself. Growth takes time.

about.quotes.8: Celebrate the small wins. They count too.

settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHelp: The language of this plugin's windows. Zone and item names always follow the game client.
settings.general.openOnLoginHelp: Pop the main window automatically the next time you log in.
settings.general.dragAnywhereHelp: Move the window by dragging anywhere inside it. When off, only the top bar moves it.
settings.general.autoPauseHelp: Pause the run while you are inside a duty, trial, raid, or any other instanced content, then resume it once you are back outside. Your run and session stats are kept.
settings.general.lootPricesHelp: Price the rare loot on the stat cards and in the tooltips from Universalis. While a run is going or the stats are on screen, the plugin sends Universalis your home data centre's name and the rare loot's item ids, at most every half hour. Off by default.
settings.general.tankbusterHelp: While a run is on and you play a tank, this plugin takes the personal mitigations over from the combat plugin, which then uses none by your HP. An enemy cast of 1.5 s or more aimed at you gets your job's short mitigation (Bloodwhetting, Holy Sheltron, The Blackest Night or Heart of Corundum) in the last 6 seconds of the cast. A treasure dungeon boss's tankbuster gets the short mitigation and one bigger cooldown, strongest first (Damnation before Rampart), as soon as their cooldowns allow. By your HP, the short mitigation is used under 80%, or under 50% while a boss is casting tankbusters, so it is ready for them. A bigger cooldown is used outside a tankbuster only when three or more enemies are hitting you and your HP is under 40%. Off by default.
settings.general.autoFollowLeader: Start automatically as a party member
settings.general.autoFollowLeaderHelp: Presses Start for you on a character that is in a party on your own world but does not lead it, so it runs as the leader's member (going to each dig spot the leader posts) without you starting it by hand. It starts as you join the party, and whenever the leader posts its next dig spot or a world to buy on while this plugin is not running. A Stop holds until the leader's next post. Off by default.
settings.general.autoAcceptRaiseHelp: While a run is on and your character is knocked out, a raise cast on it is accepted at once, wherever the run is waiting. A paused run leaves it to you. When off, the run still waits for a raise in a party, and you accept it yourself. On by default.
settings.general.raiseAfterFight: Raise fallen members after a fight
settings.general.raiseAfterFightHelp: As the party leader, once a fight is over, the run raises every member still knocked out within 50 m: Swiftcast, then the job's raise, or a hard cast while Swiftcast is still cooling down. If the job you play can raise, it raises on it; otherwise it changes to the job picked below and back to your gearset afterwards. The job cannot change inside a treasure dungeon, so there only a job that can raise does it. During a fight, the combat plugin raises with Swiftcast on its own while you play a healer, Summoner or Red Mage. Off by default.
settings.general.raiseJobHelp: A healer, Summoner or Red Mage the leader changes to when the job it plays cannot raise. It needs a gearset of its own, at level 18 or more for Swiftcast (64 for Red Mage's Verraise).
settings.general.raiseJobNoGearset: No gearset holds this job, so the leader cannot change to it.
settings.postRun.label: Run when the run finishes
settings.postRun.help: One command per line, each starting with a slash. They run when a run ends on its own, before the after-run action, and never after Stop or a failure.
settings.postRun.caption: Lines that do not start with a slash are skipped, so nothing is ever said in chat. Try /li home to head home or /ays m to hand off to AutoRetainer.
plugin.commandHelp:
Toggle the TreasureHelper window.
/atm start - run your maps until a stop condition: decipher, travel, dig, fight and loot
/atm stop - stop the run
/atm stopafter - stop once the map under way is done, or take that back
/atm pause - pause or resume the run
/atm dig - run the held map: travel, dig, fight the guards and loot the coffer
/atm decipher [map] - decipher the next timeworn map in your bags, or the one named
/atm buy [map] - buy the next map under its price cap on the market board, or the one named
/atm spot - show the held map's dig spot
/atm flag - flag the dig spot on the map
/atm goto spot - travel to the dig spot
/atm goto <territory> <x> <y> <z> - travel to a point (debug helper)
/atm goto stop - stop that travel
/atm tiers - list every map tier in the console
/atm target - dump the current target's BaseId
/atm config - open the settings
/atm stats - open the history
/atm log - open the console
/atm deps - open the plugins page
/atm changelog - open the changelog
/atm about - open the about page
safety.cat.repairSub: Auto-repair gear when equipped item condition drops below the threshold.
safety.cat.consumablesSub: Keep food and medicine buffs up while running maps: Well Fed is a free +3% EXP.
safety.cat.humanizerSub: Random pauses before the run acts, the way a player reacts, and periodic city breaks between maps.
safety.cat.partyInvitesSub: Auto-decline incoming party invites during a run, after a human-like delay, with an optional reply.
safety.cat.gmAlertSub: Detects nearby Game Masters and reacts: stop the bot, ping you, or take more drastic action.
safety.repair.autoRepairHelp: Between maps, when the lowest equipped item drops to or below the threshold, the plugin runs a repair. At 0% the gear stops working, so keep some margin.
safety.repair.autoRepairOff: Auto-repair is off. Enable it to configure repair.
safety.repair.thresholdHelp: Trips when the worst equipped slot reaches this condition percentage. 20% leaves comfortable margin before the 0% breakdown.
safety.repair.sourceHelp: How the repair is performed. Self-repair uses Dark Matter from your bag (no travel). NPC repair travels to your Grand Company mender.
safety.repair.selfThenNpc.name: Self, then NPC
safety.repair.selfThenNpc.detail: Use Dark Matter from your bag first; fall back to the Grand Company mender when you run out.
safety.repair.selfOnly.name: Self only
safety.repair.selfOnly.detail: Repair with Dark Matter from your bag. No travel.
safety.repair.npcOnly.name: NPC only
safety.repair.npcOnly.detail: Travel to your Grand Company mender (or a custom NPC) and repair there.
safety.repair.customNpcHelp: Optional. Travel to any repair NPC instead of the Grand Company mender. Target the NPC in-game, then click "Set from target". Clear to fall back to the GC mender.
safety.repair.npcNote: NPC repair uses your custom repair NPC if set, otherwise your Grand Company mender, teleporting there when needed. A custom NPC removes the Grand Company requirement.
safety.repair.npcNone: None: the Grand Company mender is used.
safety.repair.noTargetChat: No target. Target a repair NPC first, then click again.
safety.consumables.autoConsumeHelp: Use food and medicine between maps, at the start of each map and between treasure dungeon rounds to keep their buffs up; Well Fed alone is a free +3% EXP. Items are consumed only when out of combat, and refreshed before the buff runs out.
safety.consumables.autoConsumeOff: Auto-consume is off. Enable it to pick items.
safety.consumables.refreshUnderHelp: Re-consume once the buff has fewer than this many minutes left. 0 only re-applies after it fully wears off. A meal lasts 30 minutes.
safety.consumables.addItemHelp: Pick from the food and medicine in your bag. HQ is used automatically when you have it.
safety.consumables.activeItemsHelp: Each is kept active in order; the next available one is consumed if the first runs out.
safety.consumables.noneInBag: No food or medicine in your bag. Stock some, then add it here.
safety.consumables.noItemsAdded: No items added, so nothing will be consumed.
safety.humanizer.enableHelp: Every N maps, teleport to a random selected city and wander around for a few minutes before resuming. Helps you avoid player reports by acting a little more human, useful when you leave the PC running for long sessions and don't want others noticing you digging non-stop.
safety.humanizer.off: City breaks are off. Turn them on to set them up.
safety.humanizer.mapsBetweenHelp: Take a break after this many finished maps. The count starts over after each break, and whenever a run starts or resumes.
safety.humanizer.breakLengthHelp: A random duration between these two values is rolled for each break.
safety.humanizer.pauseBetweenHelp: After arriving at each random point, stand still for a random duration in this range before walking somewhere else.
safety.humanizer.walkDistanceHelp: Each random destination is rolled this many meters away from your current position. Larger ranges cover more of the city; smaller ranges keep you near the aetheryte.
safety.humanizer.allowedCitiesHelp: Tick the cities the plugin is allowed to teleport to. One is picked at random each break. Untick cities you haven't unlocked or don't want visited.
safety.humanizer.noCities: No cities selected, so the Humanizer skips the break and keeps going.
safety.invites.autoDeclineHelp: While a run is going, automatically decline incoming party invites after a short random delay. Invites that arrive while idle or playing manually are left alone for you to handle.
safety.invites.autoDeclineOff: Auto-decline is off. Enable it to configure it.
safety.invites.delayHelp: Wait a random time in this range before declining, so it looks like you noticed the popup and dismissed it yourself.
safety.invites.sendReplyHelp: After declining, send a chat message so it reads like a polite human brush-off rather than an instant silent decline.
safety.invites.channelHelp: Where the message goes. "Tell inviter" whispers the person who invited you. Ignored when your message starts with a slash command.
safety.invites.channelTell.name: Tell inviter
safety.invites.channelTell.detail: Whisper the person who invited you.
safety.invites.channelSay.name: Say
safety.invites.channelSay.detail: Local /say, heard by players near you.
safety.invites.channelYell.name: Yell
safety.invites.messageHelp: Use {name} for the inviter's character name and {world} for their home world. If the message begins with "/", it's sent verbatim as a command (e.g. /tell {name}@{world} busy right now!).
safety.gm.stopRunHelp: Halt automation immediately when a GM appears nearby. Strongly recommended; the rest of the alerts are useless if the bot keeps going.
safety.gm.toastHelp: Pop a Dalamud toast: "GM <name> is nearby!"
safety.gm.chatHelp: Print a red chat warning into your local log.
safety.gm.soundHelp: Plays a series of system beeps through your speakers. Loud enough to grab your attention if you're tabbed away.
safety.gm.beepCountHelp: How many beeps to play in the burst.
safety.gm.commandsHelp: Chat commands to run when a GM is spotted. Useful for things like /logout, /sh stay calm, or a macro.
safety.gm.killHelp: Hard-terminate the game process via /xlkill. The last-resort option; no goodbyes, no cutscene, no logout. You'll get a disconnect.
cleanup.catSub: Discard the loot you do not keep, so the bags never fill up during a run.
cleanup.enableHelp: Every item a coffer or a treasure dungeon gives is noted. Between maps, before walking into a portal, and once a run finishes, the noted items that are not kept are discarded from your bags. Maps and anything on the whitelist are never discarded, rare loot is kept unless you pick it below, and notable items are kept unless you turn that off. The noted list belongs to the run and the character: it is forgotten when the run stops or ends and when you log out.
cleanup.safety: Only an item the bags held none of before the coffer opened can be discarded, unless it does not stack (each copy then has a slot of its own), and never more copies than the coffer or dungeon gave. A map or dungeon you paused the run in after its coffer opened is left alone, since what you did meanwhile would look like its loot.
cleanup.off: Auto-discard is off. Nothing is noted or discarded.
cleanup.maxQuantityHelp: An item looted in a larger quantity than this is kept instead of discarded, such as a big stack of whetstones from a treasure dungeon. 0 sets no limit.
cleanup.keepNotableHelp: Never discard an item of green rarity or above, a unique item, equipment, a furnishing, or an item with a use other than a meal or a medicine (minions, mounts, orchestrion rolls, cards, hairstyles and the like). This keeps the rare loot of the maps the list below does not cover. On by default.
cleanup.addItemHelp: Search any item in the game by name or item ID. You can also right-click an item in your inventory or an item link in chat and choose "Add to cleanup whitelist".
cleanup.moreMatches.one: {0} more match; type more to narrow it down.
cleanup.moreMatches.other: {0} more matches; type more to narrow them down.
cleanup.noKept: The whitelist is empty, so all noted loot is discarded.
cleanup.rareHelp: Click an item to switch it: lit up is kept, dimmed is discarded. An item listed under more than one map or dungeon switches under all of them.
cleanup.rareWarning: Rare loot is kept by default. The lists below cover only the maps and dungeons shown; on any other map, Keep notable items is what keeps its minions, orchestrion rolls and furnishings, so leave it on unless you whitelist them. Some rare items do not stack, so each one takes a bag slot of its own, and keeping them all can fill up your bags.
cleanup.chatKept: {0} is on the cleanup whitelist and will not be discarded.
cleanup.chatUnkept: {0} was taken off the cleanup whitelist.
cleanup.chatGaveUp: Could not discard {0}; it was taken off the list.
cleanup.chatCapped: Stopped after {0} discards; the rest waits for the next cleanup.
shopping.catSub: Spend tomestones between maps through GatherBuddy Reborn's vendor lists.
shopping.enableHelp: Each tomestone stands alone. Between maps, every tomestone that has reached its own threshold has its items written to a GatherBuddy Reborn vendor list of its own and bought, and then the run goes back to the maps. Each item is bought in the quantity set below, on top of what you already hold, as far as the tomestones last.
shopping.off: Tomestone shopping is off. Nothing is bought.
shopping.independent: The three tomestones are independent: each one's list is bought only when that tomestone reaches its own threshold.
shopping.needsGatherBuddy: Needs GatherBuddy Reborn, loaded and up to date. Without it nothing is bought.
shopping.gatherBuddyReady: GatherBuddy Reborn is ready. Each tomestone gets its own list there: {0}.
shopping.thresholdHelp: Buy this tomestone's list once you hold at least this many. Off: this list is never bought.
shopping.addItemHelp: The items a vendor sells for this tomestone alone, with no other item or currency asked. Pick one and press Add; add as many as you like.
shopping.noOffers: No vendor sells anything for this tomestone.
shopping.itemsHelp: Bought on every trip: this many more than your bags, armoury and gear hold at the time.
shopping.noItems: No items yet, so this tomestone's list is skipped.
shopping.chatStart: You hold {1} {0} (threshold {2}); buying its list through GatherBuddy Reborn.
shopping.chatListFailed: GatherBuddy Reborn could not buy the list "{0}". The log has the details.
shopping.chatSkipped: GatherBuddy Reborn found no vendor for {1} item(s) of "{0}", so they were left out.
session.autoResumeHelp: If the treasure run hits an unexpected error and stops, restart it automatically (up to 3 times in 5 minutes) instead of ending it. Turn it off if you would rather have faults end the run.

maps.catSub: Which timeworn maps a run deciphers, and in which order.
maps.orderHelp: Which enabled map is deciphered next when your bags hold more than one tier.
maps.order.highest.name: Highest tier first
maps.order.highest.detail: Start with the newest expansion's maps and work down.
maps.order.lowest.name: Lowest tier first
maps.order.lowest.detail: Start with the oldest maps and clear them out of your bags first.
maps.tiersNote: Switch off any tier the run should leave in your bags. /atm decipher with a map's name still deciphers any tier by hand.
maps.fullPartyNote: Maps tagged Full party are tuned for eight players. They can be done alone, but the guards may be too much for your job and gear.
maps.underseaNote: Undersea maps are dug on the sea floor. They stay off until the plugin can dive.
maps.soloHelp: A solo map: its guards are tuned for one player.
maps.fullPartyHelp: Tuned for a full party of eight. Alone, the guards may be too much for your job and gear.
maps.underseaHelp: Every dig spot of this map lies under water, so it stays off until the plugin can dive.

decipher.noMaps: There is no timeworn map in your bags.

decipher.listNotShown: The game's map list did not open.
decipher.mapNotListed: The map was missing from the game's list.

mapRun.runHint: Travel to the dig spot, dig up the coffer, defeat its guards and loot it.
mapRun.refused.unresolved: The held map's dig spot could not be read. /atm spot writes the details to the console.
mapRun.refused.portalMap: The held map is a thief's map that leads to a portal. Portals are not handled yet, so dig it up by hand.
mapRun.refused.undersea: This map's dig spot lies under water, and the plugin cannot dive yet.
mapRun.refused.notUnlocked: Dig is not unlocked on this character yet.
mapRun.refused.inDuty: Maps cannot be dug up while you are bound by a duty.
mapRun.refused.partyNotInArea: Every party member must be in the area before the game allows a dig.
mapRun.refused.boundByDuty: The game refused the dig because you are bound by another duty.
mapRun.refused.partyBoundByDuty: The game refused the dig because a party member is bound by another duty.
mapRun.refused.portalDug: The dig turned up a teleportation portal. Turn on Dungeons > Enter the portal to have the run take it solo, or enter it by hand.
mapRun.refused.cofferPrompt: The coffer's confirmation did not read as expected, so it was declined.
mapRun.refused.notCombatClass: Switch to a combat job first: a crafter or gatherer cannot fight off the coffer's guards.
mapRun.chat.looted.one: {1}: coffer looted for {2} gil and {0} item.
mapRun.chat.looted.other: {1}: coffer looted for {2} gil and {0} items.
mapRun.chat.portal: A portal appeared. It is left alone, so enter it by hand if you want the dungeon.
mapRun.rollHelp: How the run answers the game's Need or Greed window for the coffer's items that are rolled for.
mapRun.roll.need.name: Need
mapRun.roll.need.detail: Roll Need on every item that allows it, and Greed where Need is not allowed.
mapRun.roll.greed.name: Greed
mapRun.roll.pass.name: Pass
mapRun.roll.pass.detail: Pass on every item, so the rest of the party can have it.
mapRun.roll.manual.name: Leave it to me
mapRun.roll.manual.detail: Do not roll. The window stays open for you to answer.
humanizer.enabledHelp: Wait a random moment before each action below, drawn anew each time between the shortest and the longest value. A shortest value above the longest is used as a fixed wait. Off acts at once.
humanizer.moveOffHelp: Once a map is in hand, before the run sets out for its dig spot.
humanizer.teleportHelp: Before each teleport the run casts: on the way to a dig spot, to a repair or to a city break.
humanizer.digHelp: Once at the dig spot, before each use of Dig.
humanizer.openCofferHelp: Once beside the coffer the dig turned up, before opening it.
humanizer.engageHelp: Once the coffer has opened and its guards appear, before joining the fight. Cut short when the character is under attack at half health or less.
market.enabled: Buy maps on the market board
market.enabledHelp: When your bags hold no enabled map and no daily map can be gathered, the run travels to a market board, buys the cheapest map under its tier's price cap, then deciphers and runs it.
market.off: Off. Runs use only the maps already in your bags.
market.budgetHelp: The most gil one run spends on maps, market tax included. Once it is spent, the run stops buying.
market.keepGilHelp: A map is never bought if it would leave you with less gil than this.
market.boardHelp: The market board the run travels to. A board a few steps away is used wherever you stand.
market.board.auto.name: Automatic
market.board.auto.detail: Limsa Lominsa Lower Decks, or Old Sharlayan while you are there: both boards are a short walk from the city aetheryte.
market.board.aetheryte.detail: The board is a short walk from the city aetheryte.
market.board.aethernet.detail: The board is reached with an aethernet ride inside the city.
market.board.district.detail: The board stands in another district of the city, reached through the aethernet.
market.crossWorldHelp: Before each purchase in a run, look up the map's price across your data centre on Universalis (the plugin sends it the data centre's name and the map's item id) and travel with Lifestream to the world that sells it cheapest. The board there is read again, and the map is dug on that world. When the run ends, the character travels back to the world it started on, unless it logs out or closes the game. In a party on your own world, the leader posts the world in party chat, breaks the party up, and every member travels there; once the leader has bought, it invites them back and the run goes on on that world. Never in a party you do not lead, and never for a purchase outside a run. Without Lifestream, maps are bought where you stand. Off by default.
market.crossWorldSavingsHelp: Travel only when the other world sells the map at least this much cheaper than your current world.
market.crossWorldNoLifestream: Lifestream is not loaded, so maps are bought on the world you stand on.
market.buyAheadHelp: After buying a map, decipher it at the board and buy a second one into your bags, so the next map needs no trip to the board. The second map counts against the budget like any other. Off by default.
market.spareFirst: Buy a spare before the first dig
market.spareFirstHelp: When a run starts with a deciphered map but no spare in your bags, buy the spare at the board before digging, so the map after it needs no trip of its own. It spends gil like any purchase. Off by default.
market.capsNote: The most a run pays for one map of each tier, before the market tax. A tier without a cap is never bought, and neither is a tier switched off below. Only tradable tiers are listed.
market.capHelp: The highest price per map accepted for this tier, before the market tax. 0 leaves the tier unbought.
market.reason.off: Market buying is off. Settings, Maps turns it on.
market.reason.unsupported: The market board's functions were not found in this game version.
market.reason.freeTrial: Free trial accounts cannot use the market board.
market.reason.inDuty: The market board cannot be used while you are bound by a duty.
market.reason.stopped: Buying stopped for this run: the game said there was not enough gil.
market.reason.noCaps: No enabled, tradable map tier has a price cap. Settings, Maps sets them.
market.reason.allHeld: Your bags already hold a map of every tier with a price cap, and only one of each fits.
market.reason.budgetSpent: The run's market budget is spent.
market.reason.notEnoughGil: Not enough gil: a map at its price cap would leave less than the gil to keep.
market.reason.boardLocked: The chosen market board is out of reach: its city aetheryte is not attuned, or the board is not unlocked yet.
market.fail.board: The market board could not be reached or opened.
market.fail.throttled: The market board kept asking to wait. Try again in a little while.
market.fail.interfered: Another search took over the market board.
market.fail.listingsChanged: The listings kept changing before a purchase went through.
market.fail.notLanded: The game accepted the purchase, but the map never reached your bags.

market.fail.unexpected: An unexpected error stopped it. The Console has the details.

market.chat.inBags: {0} is already in your bags, and only one fits.
market.buyMapHint: Buy the next map under its price cap on the market board.
gather.enabledHelp: Once a day the game lets each character gather one timeworn map as a Miner or Botanist. When the run has no map left, it switches to the gatherer's gearset, gathers the map, switches back to your gearset and deciphers it.
gather.gathererHelp: Which class gathers the map. Its gearset is found by class, wherever it sits in your gearset list.
gather.gatherer.automatic.name: Automatic
gather.gatherer.automatic.detail: Whichever of your Miner and Botanist gearsets has the higher level, the Botanist on a tie.
gather.gatherer.miner.name: Miner
gather.gatherer.botanist.name: Botanist
gather.visitsHelp: How many nodes one attempt opens before it gives up until the next run. A node shows the map only by chance, so a node without it is gathered out to bring up the next one.
gather.tierNote: The map gathered is the highest enabled tier the gatherer's level allows, skipping tiers already in your bags. A Miner skips one level 100 tier, as its only Miner nodes hold nothing but collectables. Map tiers below chooses which tiers are enabled.
gather.reason.off: Gathering the daily map is switched off.
gather.reason.unknown: The daily map allowance has not been read from the server yet.
gather.reason.notYet: The next daily map can be gathered in {0}.
gather.reason.noGearset: No Miner or Botanist gearset was found. Save one in the gearset list first.
gather.reason.noMinerGearset: No Miner gearset was found. Save one in the gearset list first.
gather.reason.noBotanistGearset: No Botanist gearset was found. Save one in the gearset list first.
gather.reason.levelTooLow: The gatherer's level is below every enabled map tier it could gather.
gather.reason.noEnabledTier: None of the map tiers a gatherer can find is enabled in Settings, Maps.
gather.reason.alreadyHeld: Your bags already hold every map tier the gatherer could gather, and only one of each fits.
gather.reason.inCombat: The character stayed in combat, so the gearset could not be changed.

gather.reason.travelFailed: Could not reach the gathering area.
gather.reason.noNode: No gathering node of the area could be found.
gather.reason.noMap: None of the nodes opened showed the map. The next run tries again.
gather.reason.limitReached: The game says today's map has already been gathered.
gather.reason.alreadyCarrying: You already carry that map, and only one fits.
gather.reason.rateZero: The map's gathering rate is 0%. The gatherer's Gathering stat is too low.
gather.reason.notConfirmed: The game never confirmed the map was gathered.
gather.reason.attacked: The gatherer was attacked, so it left the area instead of fighting.
gather.reason.switchBackFailed: Could not switch back to your gearset. Switch back by hand before going on.

gather.commandHelp:
/atm gather - gather today's timeworn map once as a Miner or Botanist
/atm gather stop - stop the gathering
gather.reason.noReturnGearset: No gearset holds the class you are on, so the gather could not switch you back. Save one in the gearset list first.
dungeon.commandHelp:
/atm dungeon - clear the treasure dungeon you stand in (solo only)
/atm dungeon record - start writing what the dungeon shows to a file
/atm dungeon record stop - stop the recording
/atm dungeon nearby - list the objects around you in the console
dungeon.chat.unverified: This dungeon has not been checked in game yet. Stay close, and if it goes wrong, /atm dungeon record while you clear it by hand helps fix it.
dungeon.chat.notInDungeon: You are not in a treasure dungeon the plugin knows. It knows Cenote Ja Ja Gural and Vault Oneiron so far.
dungeon.chat.inParty: Treasure dungeons are only cleared solo for now. Leave the party first.
dungeon.chat.stuck: The dungeon shows nothing the plugin knows how to act on, so the rest is up to you.
dungeon.chat.notOurDungeon: The run did not enter this treasure dungeon, so it is up to you (/atm dungeon clears it). The run carries on once you are back outside.
dungeon.chat.lootWaiting: Items still wait on a roll, so the run leaves the dungeon to you rather than lose them.
dungeon.chat.nearbyWritten: {0} object(s) nearby written to the console (/atm log).
dungeon.chat.lure: The Gambler's Lure is up. Make your choice; the run goes on once the lure is over.
dungeon.chat.bonusRound: A bonus round began. Pick up the glowing sacks yourself; the run goes on once it ends.
dungeon.chat.enteringPortal: A portal appeared. Entering it to clear the treasure dungeon.
dungeon.chat.portalNotEntered: The run could not get into the portal, so the dungeon is left to you.
dungeon.chat.portalInParty: A portal appeared, but you are in a party, so the dungeon is left to you.
dungeon.chat.unknownDungeon: This treasure dungeon is not one the plugin can clear yet, so it is up to you. The run carries on once you are back outside.
dungeon.chat.recordStarted: Recording the dungeon to {0}. Clear it by hand, then /atm dungeon record stop.
dungeon.chat.lureCapture: The Gambler's Lure window is being written down to {0}.
dungeon.chat.lureRare: The coffer holds rare loot ({0}), so the treasure is taken as it is rather than challenged blind.
dungeon.chat.lureTake: Gambler's Lure: taking the treasure at {0}x.
dungeon.chat.lureBlindGuess: Gambler's Lure: no one guessed within a minute and the card could not be read, so the run guessed {0} at random to keep the treasure from being lost. The rest of this run takes the coffers as they are.
dungeon.chat.lureCardHint: Gambler's Lure: the card shows {0}; guess {1}.
dungeon.catSub: Gates and the Gambler's Lure inside treasure dungeons
dungeon.enterPortalHelp: When a coffer leaves a portal behind, or a dig turns one up, walk into it and clear the treasure dungeon, then carry on with the next map. Solo, or as the leader of a party on your own world whose members run this plugin; in any other party the portal is left to you. Off by default.
dungeon.gatePolicyHelp: Which gate the run opens in a dungeon that makes you choose one. It applies to every gate dungeon unless one is set on its own below.
dungeon.gate.random.name: Random
dungeon.gate.random.detail: Pick one of the gates at random each time.
dungeon.gate.left.name: Left
dungeon.gate.left.detail: Always the leftmost gate, as seen from the chamber.
dungeon.gate.right.name: Right
dungeon.gate.right.detail: Always the rightmost gate, as seen from the chamber.
dungeon.gate.default.name: As above
dungeon.gate.default.detail: Follow the gate to try set above.
dungeon.followHintHelp: When the game lights one of the gates, open that one whatever the setting above says.
dungeon.perDungeonHelp: The gate to try in this dungeon only.
dungeon.preferBonusHelp: Rare enemies that drop extra loot and run off if left too long, such as the goldy cat and the vaultkeeper, are attacked before anything else.
dungeon.perDungeonBonusHelp: Not first leaves this dungeon's bonus enemies to the usual order, so the other enemies are not left hitting you.
dungeon.bonus.first.name: Attack first
dungeon.bonus.first.detail: Bonus enemies are attacked before anything else here.
dungeon.bonus.last.name: Not first
dungeon.bonus.last.detail: Bonus enemies are fought like the rest here, so the other enemies are not left hitting you.
dungeon.mandragorasInOrder: Kill the mandragora party in order
dungeon.mandragorasInOrderHelp: The five mandragoras are killed by the numbers over their heads: onion, eggplant, garlic, tomato, then the queen. With both settings on, bonus enemies still come first.
dungeon.mandragorasSoloNote: Not recommended solo: area attacks and the rotation's own picks can kill them out of order, which loses the full reward.
dungeon.lurePolicyHelp: A coffer can come with the Gambler's Lure, a high-or-low game that can multiply its treasure or lose all of it.
dungeon.lure.ask.name: Let me choose
dungeon.lure.ask.detail: The run waits while you play it or open the coffer yourself.
dungeon.lure.open.name: Open the coffer
dungeon.lure.open.detail: Take the treasure as it is and skip the game.
dungeon.lure.auto.name: Challenge by the loot
dungeon.lure.auto.detail: Takes the first challenge unless the coffer holds rare loot the cleanup keeps, then weighs each next one on its card, since the card turned over becomes the next one to guess on. Without rare loot it plays for the most on average; with it, it goes on only on a card of 1 to 3 or 7 to 9. Each guess is made on the card: 1 to 4 high, 6 to 9 low.
